title: add-dependency-health-gate-and-slim-builder-for-ci-images
author: Priya Narayanan
release_notes: Introduce a pre-merge dependency-health gate to fail PRs with high-severity unresolved vulnerabilities and add a slim multi-stage builder image to reduce CI image size and speed up workflows. No user-facing runtime changes.
description: Motivation: CI has been brittle due to three root causes: transient dependency vulnerabilities that slip through until release, long docker build times and cache churn from large base images, and duplicated build steps across workflows. This PR introduces a lightweight pre-merge 'dependency-health' gate and a slim multi-stage CI builder image that other workflows can reuse. The dependency gate runs fast checks (lockfile integrity, top-level license issues, and a vulnerability scan that flags critical/urgent CVEs). The slim builder reduces image size by removing dev-only packages and consolidating language runtimes into a single, cache-friendly layer. The goal is to reduce CI flakiness, cut median CI image build time by ~40%, and prevent high-severity vulnerabilities from reaching main. Summary of changes: - Add .github/workflows/dependency-health.yml: pre-merge job that runs lockfile-check, dep-tree-lint, oss-vuln-scan and posts a clear status and remediation hints. - Add docker/ci/Dockerfile.slim: multi-stage builder that uses the current official base but extracts only runtime artifacts and installs tooling in a separate layer to maximize cache reuse. - Update .github/workflows/ci-lint.yml and ci-test.yml to use the slim builder image from the registry for build/test steps; fall back to local build when registry image is not available. - Add scripts/dep-health.sh and scripts/fix-lockfile.sh for consistent checks across CI and local dev. - Update ci/README.md with instructions to run the dependency gate locally and how to regenerate the slim image. - Small helper: .github/actions/cache-keying: tweak to include slim image tag so cache hits are more reliable. Checklist: - [x] Add dependency-health workflow and scripts - [x] Add multi-stage slim Dockerfile and publish step in ci-builder workflow - [x] Wire existing CI jobs to use slim image when available - [x] Add helpful failure messages and remediation links - [x] Update docs and READMEs - [x] Add tests for lockfile-check script Commits (high-level): 1) add dependency-health workflow and basic scripts (dep-health.sh, fix-lockfile.sh) 2) introduce docker/ci/Dockerfile.slim and builder workflow 3) hook workflows (ci-lint, ci-test) to try pulling the slim image and fallback to local build 4) CI cache-keying tweaks + docs Updates to files (high-level): - .github/workflows/dependency-health.yml (new) - .github/workflows/ci-builder.yml (new step to publish slim image) - .github/workflows/ci-lint.yml (modified to pull slim image) - .github/workflows/ci-test.yml (modified to pull slim image) - docker/ci/Dockerfile.slim (new) - scripts/dep-health.sh (new) - scripts/fix-lockfile.sh (new) - ci/README.md (updated) - .github/actions/cache-keying/action.yml (tweaked) Review conversation (abridged): - Ethan Cole (review): "Nice approach. A couple of questions: can the vuln scan be rate-limited? also we should avoid failing PRs on moderate severities until we have a triage path." - Author (Priya): "Good points. The oss-vuln-scan is configured to only fail on CRITICAL/URGENT by default; I've added a flag to optionally escalate MODERATE for high-risk repos, but the default is conservative. Added docs that explain how to change the threshold via repo settings." - Marta Rossi (review): "Slim image looks good. I hit a missing build-tool in the slim image when running tests locally (node-gyp)." - Author: "Thanks — added a small build-tools layer for optional dev-only dependencies that is present in the CI image but not in runtime images. The ci-builder publishes two tags: :slim and :slim-dev; workflows pick :slim first and fall back to :slim-dev if a dev-step needs compilation." - Jinsoo Park (review): "Lockfile checksum check is great. We should make the output machine-readable for automation (JSON)." - Author: "Updated dep-health.sh to emit a compact JSON summary when CI sets REPORT_JSON=1, and the workflow uploads it as an artifact for easier triage." CI run history (selected): - First run (on creation): dependency-health job passed, builder publish failed due to registry creds (CI failed) - Push fix (add secret lookup): second run passed dependency-health and successfully published :slim-dev but failed a lint step because cache key missed (cache-miss increased time) - Final run (after cache-key tweak): all CI jobs passed; ci-lint and ci-test used pulled :slim image and median build time on the PR pipeline dropped ~43% measured across 10 runs. Edge cases and notes: - For forks: dependency-health is run in a reduced-mode that only runs local checks (no secret access for publishing); this was documented and the workflow early-returns with a clear message. - Renovate: I added a note in ci/README to recommend enabling renovate's "pr-body" policy so dependency gate output is easier to find on automated updates. - Rollout plan: enable the gate as required for all non-trivial repos (redwood/*) in a staged fashion; initially opt-in for 'redwood-examples' and 'redwood-sdk-*' to monitor false positives. - Security: oss-vuln-scan is a thin wrapper around our internal vulnerability provider; no secrets were added to the scripts; scanning is done via public CVE feeds and the results are solely used to set a PR status. - Backwards compatibility: workflows fall back to the prior local build path when the slim image pull fails. Testing performed: - Local run of dep-health.sh against a purposely modified lockfile to ensure failure path returns non-zero and produces a JSON report. - End-to-end run on the PR with builder publish to staging registry. - Manual smoke test of ci-lint and ci-test pulling the slim image. Next steps (post-merge): - Roll the dependency-health gate to more repositories and add a dashboard showing gate failures by repo. - Add automated annotations that link failing CVEs to remediation tips in the PR UI. - Consider auto-PR creation for safe upgrades (majority non-breaking) once we have triage rules. Overall this PR is primarily CI/ops-level change: no application code changes. It consolidates a few CI patterns and introduces a safety gate to reduce risk from dependency churn.
